ETHFI to Fully Exit EigenLayer Restaking as Yields Dry Up and Sector Profitability Declines ETHFI will sever its remaining structural ties with EigenLayer this quarter, citing a lack of meaningful additional yield relative to the risks of restaking. Less than 1% of its assets remained restaked as of August, while weETH has already removed restaking and now functions as a standard liquid staking token. Users seeking restaking exposure must opt into a separate product built on Symbiotic. DefiLlama data showed the restaking sector held $10.02 billion in TVL on September 8 but generated only about $100,000 in weekly fees, compared with $27.35 million generated by liquid staking on $51.87 billion in TVL. Excluding ETHFI, Renzo, Kelp, Swell, Puffer Finance and Bedrock generated a combined $953,350 in gross profit in Q2 2026, down from $2.18 million three quarters earlier. The sector has faced weaker economics as points incentives ended, EigenLayer activated slashing, and the Kelp bridge exploit highlighted additional cross-chain security risks. — link

NEAR Intents Blocks Over $50M in Bitget Hack Flows and Waives Recovery Bounty Share Aurora co-founder Alex Shevchenko said attackers behind the September 24 Bitget hack attempted to move more than $50 million in stolen funds through NEAR Intents. Its SHIELD risk system detected the flows, with about $166,000 passing through and roughly $503,000 frozen mid-execution pending legal and recovery procedures. Shevchenko said about $387.5 million was stolen in total, with most cross-chain funds ultimately consolidated into ETH on Ethereum. Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said NEAR Intents has waived its share of the recovery bounty to allow Bitget to recover more of the stolen funds. She added that public blockchains do not have to choose between openness and restricting known stolen funds, arguing that risk-detection mechanisms can be built in while keeping access permissionless. Bitget will proceed through the appropriate legal and asset-recovery process. — link

Coinbase Receives CFTC Approval for Derivatives Clearinghouse Coinbase said the CFTC approved Coinbase Clearing LLC as a registered Derivatives Clearing Organization (DCO), completing its CFTC-regulated derivatives stack alongside its FCM and DCM. The clearinghouse will support USDC collateral and 24/7 settlement, allowing Coinbase to directly create and settle fully collateralized contracts. — link

SlowMist CISO: Critical Apple Update May Patch Zero-Day Vulnerability Used to Drain Crypto Wallets SlowMist Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) 23pds stated that Apple has released a critical security update, which likely patches a zero-day vulnerability actively exploited to drain cryptocurrency wallets. Apple acknowledged a report indicating that the issue may have been exploited in extremely sophisticated attacks against specific targeted individuals, affecting iOS versions prior to iOS 27. — link
